index.title: Ocearo — the open-source 3D sailing display for Signal K
index.description: See your boat, the sea and the traffic in live 3D. Sail trim, COLREG advice, man overboard, anchor watch, bathymetry and weather on any screen on board. Open source, runs on a Raspberry Pi.

demo.title: Live demo — try Ocearo in your browser
demo.description: Open the real Ocearo app in your browser, fed with simulated Signal K data: the 3D view, AIS traffic, dashboard and settings. Nothing to install.

features.title: Everything you need to know, at a glance.
features.lead: Chartplotters show lines on a map. Ocearo shows what is really happening around your boat, the way a self-driving car shows the road: your boat, the wind, the sea state, the other vessels and what each of them must do.

f3d.title: Your boat, the sea and the seabed, live.
f3d.lead: A real-time 3D scene centred on your boat, built from your own instruments. One button switches between five views of the world around it.

ticks.b: A sea built from the true wind.
ticks.text: Wind sea and swell, whitecaps from 7 knots, the sun where it really is and your own wake.
OpenStreetMap and OpenSeaMap lights and marks, true to scale with the AIS targets.
SHOM 5–20 m surveys on the French coast, soundings at the current tide, shallow water against your draft hatched in orange.

colreg.eyebrow: Traffic and the rules of the road
colreg.title: Who gives way? Ocearo tells you.
colreg.lead: Every AIS target is drawn as its real ship type and size, glides between reports, and is coloured by who must keep clear — with the rule and the alteration to make.

ticks.text: from each target’s AIS status and type and from your own: under sail, a yacht is not the same vessel as under engine.
“Avoid: 15° to port”, the closest point of approach on a dashed line, and a warning when no single alteration clears everyone.
“Collision danger: LE PERTUIS at 0.5 miles… pass astern of her.”

vision.title: Today an extra pair of eyes. Tomorrow, the pilot.
vision.lead: Ocearo stands for Ocean Robot. Like a self-driving car learns to see the road, Ocearo is learning to see the sea — and, step by step, to sail with you.

steps.title: An aid to the watch
steps.text: A live picture of the boat and the traffic, the rules of the road worked out for every target, spoken alerts, anchor and man-overboard watch.

steps.title: Seeing with cameras
steps.text: Ocearo Vision, in development, uses on-board cameras to spot what AIS does not show — small boats, buoys, floating obstacles — to read the sails’ trim and to guide you into the berth.

steps.title: Autopilot by vision
steps.text: A pilot that keeps the watch, applies the rules of the road and steers through the Signal K autopilot — with the skipper always in command.

install.title: Up and running in five minutes.
install.lead: Ocearo is a Signal K webapp. If your boat already runs Signal K, you are one click away.
install.s1: Signal K server ≥ 2: Appstore → Available → ocearo-ui, or from the command line.
install.s2: Restart the server and open Ocearo on any screen on board: chart table, tablet or phone.
install.s3: Add Ocearo Core for the logbook, anchor watch, SHOM bathymetry, spoken alerts and the AI copilot.
install.ui: The 3D display, dashboard and every view. Runs in the browser.
install.core: Voice, collision watch, anchor, bathymetry and logbook on the Signal K server.
install.sk: The open marine data server that connects NMEA 0183, NMEA 2000 and more.

items.a: Yes, under the Apache 2.0 licence. The code of Ocearo UI and Ocearo Core is on GitHub: you can read it, adapt it to your boat and contribute.
A Signal K server, which a Raspberry Pi 4 or 5 runs comfortably, connected to your instruments (NMEA 2000 or 0183). Any recent browser on a tablet, phone or chart-table screen is a display.

Yes. Your instruments, AIS and the 3D view need no internet. Chart tiles, wind forecasts and bathymetry are kept on board whenever you have a connection, and can be downloaded for the area before you leave.

items.q: Is it a certified navigation system?
items.a: No. Ocearo is an aid to the watch, like a second pair of eyes. Keep a proper lookout and use official charts; the skipper stays responsible for the boat.
Any boat that publishes standard Signal K data: sailing yachts, catamarans and motor boats. The 3D view offers a 10.8 m racer, a 14 m catamaran and simpler models.
Twelve: English, French, German, Spanish, Italian, Dutch, Portuguese, Danish, Swedish, Finnish, Polish and Greek, with metric, imperial or nautical units.

Mostly with AI coding assistants, in the interest of transparency. The author, a developer and sailor, decides what the app does, reviews the changes and tests it on board, on the boat it is developed on. Code reviews and bug reports on GitHub are especially welcome.

brand.title: The Ocearo brand.
brand.lead: How the Ocearo name, mark and colours are built, and how to use them. For articles, videos, partners and contributors.
brand.logo_text: The logo is the word OCEARO in which the O is the compass of the 3D view and the A is a bow splitting the horizon. Use the dark version on dark backgrounds and the light version on light ones.
brand.alt_dark: Ocearo logo on a dark background
brand.alt_light: Ocearo logo on a light background
brand.build_text: Every part of the logo comes from the app itself.

build.text: of the 3D view, tilted 60° in perspective like the ring that floats around the boat, with its bezel, its twelve graduations fading towards the back and the own boat at its centre.
heads 045, towards the rest of the name: white jib, Ocearo-blue mainsail, standing in its centreline plane.
two blades meeting at the stem, the horizon line in Ocearo blue passing behind and cut where they touch.
are Geist Regular in capitals, tracked at 0.34 em, like the labels of the instrument panel (SOG, HEADING, TWS).
at 48 px and below the compass is shown flat, face-on, with the two sails, so it stays sharp.

brand.space_text: Keep a clear space around the logo at least as wide as the letter C. Never place it closer to an edge or to other elements.
brand.color_text: A near-black ground and one luminous blue. Red, green, violet and yellow are reserved for meaning — danger, starboard, their move, caution — and never used for decoration.
brand.type_text: Geist, by Vercel, under the SIL Open Font Licence. One family for everything; Geist Mono for coordinates and data.
brand.type_display: Your boat, the sea and the traffic, in live 3D.
brand.type_body: Ocearo turns the boat’s data into a calm, live picture of the boat, the sea and the traffic around it.
brand.ui_text: The look of the app and of everything around it.

ui.text: A dark, quiet screen; only what needs attention lights up.
Ocearo blue marks the own boat and the actions. Everything else is white or grey.
Red, violet, orange and green follow the COLREG and navigation-light conventions, everywhere.
Large values, small spaced labels, tabular figures.
Screenshots and videos come from the app with real data, never mock-ups or stock photos.

brand.rules_text: The logo is always used as supplied.
brand.r_ok: As supplied, on a plain background
brand.voice_text: Ocearo speaks like a good crew member: short, factual, calm. Sailing words, not software words.
